The rational consumer maximizes net benefit by comparing the extra (marginal) benefit of one more cookie with the extra (marginal) cost of that cookie.  
- If marginal benefit > marginal cost, eating another cookie raises net benefit.  
- If marginal benefit < marginal cost, eating another cookie lowers net benefit.  
- The optimal stopping point is where the two are equal; any further cookie would make marginal cost exceed marginal benefit.

Thus the consumer stops when **the marginal benefit equals the marginal cost of the next cookie**.

**Final answer: (B)**
